subject: Leadership readout: NovaCare buying path & procurement risks
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@novacare.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Leadership readout: NovaCare buying path & procurement risks

Hi Oliver — thanks again for carving time today.

Quick recap from our discovery and the leadership discussion you promised to run back to your exec sponsor (Maya):

Pain points / impact (as stated by NovaCare)
- Latency spikes at >95th percentile during morning batch jobs causing ingestion throttles and delayed downstream alerts (cost: estimated $40k/mo in remediation).
- Unpredictable per-token spend and difficulty forecasting month-end costs during campaigns.
- Need for private deployment options (VPC + KMS) for PHI-adjacent workloads; legal will require SOC 2 + contract terms.

Desired business outcomes
- 99th percentile gen latency < 600ms for 512-token inference at baseline traffic.
- Predictable monthly cost envelope with automated alerts when spend forecast exceeds threshold.
- Managed private deployment with customer-managed KMS and audit logs for compliance.

Procurement path / timeline (what we heard)
- Executive sponsorship confirmation this week (Maya)
- Legal & security review (SOC 2 artifacts + KMS plan) week of 6/7
- Procurement/PO decision targeted by end of June (customer preferred)

Risks / escalation items
- Legal requires SOC 2 Type II before we can sign for on-prem/private env. We can provide current reports but may need an attestation addendum.
- Data residency: Maya asked about keeping key material in us-east only.
- SLA exceptions around guaranteed throughput during peak batch windows.

Next steps (owners + dates)
1) Laura: send technical Q&A pack + mutual action plan (attached) — today (sent) — attachment: redwood-technical-answers.pdf, RWI-1349-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
2) Oliver: confirm who on NovaCare legal/security will own the SOC2 checklist and provide contact — by 6/2
3) Karthik: prepare draft SLA options and exception language for peak batch windows — by 6/4
4) Ben: schedule procurement-readout call with procurement lead once legal contact is known — target 6/7

If helpful, we can set a 30-minute readout next week with Karthik to walk security through the KMS/attestations and the SLA cheat-sheet.

Laura
Laura Bennett | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: redwood-technical-answers.pdf (summary), RWI-1349-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP milestones & owners)

From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@novacare.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@novacare.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Leadership readout: NovaCare buying path & procurement risks

Thanks Laura — useful summary. Two quick clarifications and a procurement contact:

1) Procurement/legal owner: Rachel Ortiz (rachel.ortiz@novacare.com) will own contract redlines and the SOC2 checklist. She prefers to see the attestation and our KMS integration diagram up front.
2) Data residency: we need confirmation that keys and logs for the private deployment can be pinned to us-east-1 only. If not, this becomes a blocker for our PHI-adjacent workflows.

Agree with your timeline — we should aim to have procurement looped the week of 6/7. I can confirm Maya will review the executive readout and revert by 6/2.

I attached Rachel's procurement intake template (procurement_intake_novacare.xlsx) and pasted her preferred availability for next week below. Can Ben choose two slots and we'll lock one?

Rachel's availability (PST):
- Tue 6/8 10:00-11:00
- Wed 6/9 14:00-15:00
- Thu 6/10 09:00-10:00

Oliver

Thanks — looping in briefly. I reviewed the technical Q&A and the mutual action plan. Two commitments from our side:

- SLA options: I will draft 3 graded SLA templates (standard, premium, premium-plus with peak throughput commitments and a short term exception addendum) and circulate by EOD 6/4. These will include measurable 95/99/99.9 latency targets and conditional credits tied to packetized throughput failures.
- KMS / residency: we can support a customer-managed KMS in us-east-1 and will supply a diagram and policy excerpt for Rachel to review by 6/7.

Ben — can you pick two of Oliver's suggested slots (6/8 10:00, 6/9 14:00, 6/10 09:00) and book a 30-min procurement readout. I'll join the call to walk through the SLA items.

Laura — once Rachel sends the procurement intake we should attach the SOC2 evidence pack (redwood-technical-answers.pdf includes the SOC pointers) and point to the DocuSign envelope if they want to start redlines in parallel.

Karthik
